1# Coincidence calculations and validation baseline
2
3Audit date: 2026-09-09. Manuscript: `APS_Coincidence_Algebra-14.pdf`.
4Code baseline: `3135c8757999b13288ced0978f8907a1fa87092c` plus the changes
5accompanying this document. This is a computational audit of the implemented
6products and detector model, not a proof of all bundle statements or a comparison
7with experiment/Geant4. The manuscript itself has not been changed.
8
9## Supported mathematics
10
11`CAlgebra` implements the ordered product of Eqs. (41)-(45). Its connection is
12
13    c_d(x,y) = sum over paths t(x) -> s(y) of product of tau edge coefficients.
14
15The zero-length connection is 1. Initial populations do not enter this scalar;
16they enter separately through `Embed(b)`. Thus `b *_d tau^k` gives each ordered
17k-transition coincidence once, retaining initial-level markers where the
18stationary quotient permits. Sum coefficients over initial markers for a given
19transition set. Do not divide by k! or count the reversed order again in this
20strictly descending algebra. Summing all pair coefficients gives an expected
21number of pairs per decay, not necessarily a probability bounded by one.
22
23The existing tests check associativity including stationary and disconnected
24factors. The new tests independently enumerate completed physical cascades and
25all observed subsets, comparing every coefficient of Eq. (61) and Eq. (70).
26They cover parallel edges, two sinks, mixed initial populations, IC, zero/perfect
27peak efficiencies and N=1,2,4. Exact detector assignment enumeration separately
28checks the two-detector avoidance argument below.
29
30The path/coincidence correspondence is precise for **composable** paths: their
31connection is 1 and concatenation agrees with tensor composition. Embedding is
32linear, but is NOT a global algebra homomorphism: two separated paths have zero
33path-algebra product and may have nonzero coincidence product. `PathForm` uses
34endpoint equivalence, whereas coincidence basis equality retains transition
35identity. Parallel arrows must not be inadvertently merged when selecting a
36specific transition.
37
38## Detection maps and the chosen fiber
39
40For physical gamma-plus-IC branches x_e, gamma fraction q_e=1/(1+alpha_e),
41whole-array conditional peak efficiency p_e and total efficiency t_e:
42
43    h_e = x_e q_e p_e
44    o_e(m) = x_e (1 - m q_e t_e/N)
45
46`FullEnergyHit` supplies h. `SummingOut` supplies o(1).
47`AvoidDetectors(tau,m)` supplies o(m), requiring 0 <= m <= N.
48These are path-algebra diagonal maps, extended multiplicatively along paths.
49Stationary paths are unchanged; branches are not renormalized.
50
51`FullEnergyHit`, `TotalHit`, and `SummingOut` also accept `CAlgebra::Vector`.
52Those overloads act only on the explicitly observed factors and preserve
53stationary markers. They commute with path embedding. They do **not** replace
54the base vector stored in a CAlgebra. In a fixed fiber they respect its product;
55transport to a different detection-mapped fiber generally does not preserve
56products, because hidden connecting transitions acquire different weights.
57
58For independent detection without summing corrections:
59
60```cpp
61CAlgebra physical(quiver, order, b + tau);
62auto pairs = physical.Multiply(physical.Embed(b),
63                              physical.Power(physical.Embed(tau), 2));
64auto detected = maps.FullEnergyHit(pairs);
65```
66
67For Eq. (70), including sums between disconnected transitions:
68
69```cpp
70CAlgebra out(quiver, order, maps.SummingOut(tau));
71auto H = maps.SummingInExpansion(out, tau); // original physical tau
72// H = h + h *_out h/N + h *_out h *_out h/N^2 + ...
73auto spectrum = out.Multiply(out.Multiply(out.Embed(b), H), out.Embed(E));
74```
75
76E is the sum of stationary paths at all physical terminal levels (one ground
77state in the paper). The same out fiber supplies avoidance before, between and
78after observed factors. Each coefficient is the expected number of the specified
79single-detector peak events per decay. Different detectors can contribute
80multiple counts in one decay. This is not a normalized exclusive event vector.
81The path-algebra expansion contains only connected observed paths; the
82coincidence expansion additionally retains disconnected sums.
83
84## Two distinct clean peaks
85
86For two individually resolved transitions with no summed-in photons in either
87peak, all other emissions must avoid **both** selected detectors:
88
89```cpp
90// N >= 2; for N == 1 this observable is identically zero.
91CAlgebra twoOut(quiver, order, maps.AvoidDetectors(tau, 2));
92auto h = twoOut.Embed(maps.FullEnergyHit(tau));
93auto cleanPairs = twoOut.Multiply(
94    twoOut.Multiply(twoOut.Embed(b), twoOut.Power(h, 2)), twoOut.Embed(E));
95for (auto& term : cleanPairs)
96    term.coefficient *= double(N - 1) / double(N);
97```
98
99The prefactor selects distinct detectors. The connection uses o(2), not o(1).
100This agrees with complete-cascade enumeration in the identical independent
101isotropic detector model. It is a deliberately restricted observable, not an
102implementation of general Eq. (72) with summed-in groups and energy gates.
103Such groups need detector/group labels: a single tensor of photons does not
104record which photons summed into which peak. See CA-002 in the discrepancy
105register before using Eq. (72) as a general simulation prediction.
106
107## Reproducible sample
108
109Run from the repository root:
110
111```sh
112COINALGEBRA_HOME="$PWD" bin/coinalgebra -l -b -q examples/calculations/coincidence.C
113ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
114```
115
116The example uses A(600 keV)->B(400 keV) with probability 1, then B->C(100 keV)
117with probability .75 or B->G(0 keV) with .25, and C->G with probability 1.
118Population is entirely at A. N=4. Input responses, deliberately synthetic:
119
120| Edge | Energy (keV) | Peak | Total | alpha |
121|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
122| AB | 200 | .4 | .6 | 0 |
123| BC | 300 | .3 | .5 | 1 |
124| BG | 400 | .35 | .55 | 0 |
125| CG | 100 | .5 | .7 | .25 |
126
127For AB and CG, whose gap contains BC:
128
129| Observable | Calculation | Per decay |
130|---|---|---:|
131| Physical coincidence | .75 | .75 |
132| Independent full-energy detections | .75*.4*(.5/1.25) | .12 |
133| Two clean distinct-detector peaks | .12*(3/4)*(1-2*.5/(2*4)) | .07875 |
134| Same-detector AB+CG sum, BC avoids it | .12/4*(1-.5/(2*4)) | .028125 |
135
136The executable prints all individual basis coefficients, including singles and
137three-photon sums, so future simulation comparisons can use exactly specified
138observables. Efficiencies alone do not define summing-out: measured total
139response, detector count, and the detector grouping (crystals vs addback) must
140also match the simulation. No angular correlations, interdetector scattering,
141auxiliary conversion radiation, time windows or addback model is included.
142
143## Remaining manuscript work
144
145The Eq. (40) target discrepancy and Eq. (32) terminal boundary remain recorded;
146Eq. (70)'s explicit ground-state factor supports the implemented terminal
147convention. Bundle isomorphisms in Eqs. (49)-(58), arbitrary signed fibers, and
148general gated group detection have not been certified by this audit. Support
149alone cannot ensure positive nonzero path connections for arbitrary signed
150coefficients because different paths can cancel. The physical tests use
151nonnegative normalized branches. CAlgebra intentionally also allows general
152scalar coefficients; it does not turn arbitrary vectors into probabilities.
153
